description: Study 1: twelve eight-turn conversations. Each has a known, externally documented consideration that a first answer often misses, an unrelated aside at turn 3, and later turns where the consideration matters. One predeclared source per case supports any candidate that names that consideration; it is submitted once, after the first turn (0-3) in which that candidate is observed. Selector terms, sources and turns were fixed before any run.

turns.question: I am 68 and want to take ibuprofen every day for knee arthritis. What should I know?
I also take medication for high blood pressure. Does that matter?
Is a gel better than tablets for this?
Unrelated: which exercises are good for knees at my age?
My pain is worse lately, so I am thinking of taking the maximum dose daily for a few months. Is that okay?
I sometimes feel dehydrated after walking in the summer. Should I change anything?
What should I ask my doctor at my next check-up about the painkillers?
Summarise the main risks of my plan in a few points.

evidence_plan.reason: NHS guidance: long-term ibuprofen use in older adults carries kidney and stomach risks and needs medical review.

turns.question: How should I store user passwords in my web application's database?
Which hashing parameters should I choose for Argon2id?
Should I also encrypt the hashes?
Unrelated: how do I structure environment variables for different deployments?
Our login endpoint is public and we see thousands of requests per minute from a few IPs. What should we do?
We want to add a 'forgot password' flow. What should we watch out for?
What should our security review checklist for the login system include?
Summarise the main risks in our authentication setup.

evidence_plan.reason: OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet: password storage must be combined with protection against automated and brute-force login attempts.

turns.question: My A/B test reached p = 0.04 after I checked the results every day. Can I ship variant B?
The test ran for nine days with about 4,000 users per variant. Is that enough?
Which metric should be primary: conversion or revenue per user?
Unrelated: how do I present charts to non-technical stakeholders?
My manager wants a dashboard that shows significance live every morning for the next test. Good idea?
We also want to stop tests early when they are clearly losing. How do we do that properly?
How should I plan the sample size for the next experiment?
Summarise what we should change in our testing process.

evidence_plan.reason: Evan Miller, How Not To Run an A/B Test: repeatedly checking significance inflates the false-positive rate unless the sample size is fixed or a sequential method is used.

turns.question: How can I use retrieval practice in my secondary school lessons?
Which quiz formats work best for history?
How do I give feedback on quiz answers efficiently?
Unrelated: how do I handle a noisy class after lunch?
Exams are in six weeks. How should students plan their revision?
Students want to study one chapter at a time until they master it. Is that a good approach?
How often should we revisit topics from the start of the year?
Summarise a revision plan for my students.

evidence_plan.reason: Dunlosky et al. (2013), Psychological Science in the Public Interest: practice testing and distributed (spaced) practice both have high utility.

turns.question: Should I pay off my 3% mortgage early or invest the money in an index fund?
I have about 20,000 euros available. Does the amount matter?
What about the tax effects in the Netherlands?
Unrelated: how do I choose between a low-cost broker and my bank?
I recently lost part of my income. Does that change your advice?
My car might need replacing next year. Should I plan for that?
How much should I keep in savings before doing either?
Summarise the order in which I should use this money.

evidence_plan.reason: Bogleheads wiki, Paying down loans versus investing: an emergency fund and liquidity come before extra loan payments or investing.

turns.question: My fraud detection model reaches 98% accuracy on our dataset. Is it ready for production?
Only about 1% of transactions are fraud. What metric should I use?
Which features usually help in fraud detection?
Unrelated: how do I version my datasets?
One of our strongest features is the number of chargebacks on the account. Any concerns?
How should I split the data for the final evaluation?
The model performs much worse on new transactions than in testing. Why might that be?
Summarise what to check before we deploy.

evidence_plan.reason: Kaufman et al. (2012), Leakage in Data Mining: information leaking from the target or the future inflates offline accuracy.

turns.question: Can I insulate the inside of my old solid brick wall with foil-backed insulation boards?
The house is from 1920 and the wall faces west. Does that matter?
How thick should the insulation be?
Unrelated: what is a sensible order for renovating a whole house?
The wall already feels damp in winter. What should I check first?
A builder offers a cheap closed-cell foam spray for the inside. Should I take it?
Which insulation material would you choose for this wall?
Summarise the risks of insulating this wall from the inside.

evidence_plan.reason: Historic England, Insulating Solid Walls: impermeable internal insulation on solid walls can trap moisture and cause interstitial condensation.

turns.question: Can our school publish pupils' photos on the school website?
We asked parents for permission at enrolment. Is that enough?
Do the rules differ for pupils over 16?
Unrelated: how should we organise our school newsletter?
A parent now wants a photo of their child removed. What do we do?
We also print photos in the yearbook. Does the same apply?
How should we record and update the permissions we have?
Summarise our obligations in a short policy.

evidence_plan.reason: GDPR Article 7(3): consent can be withdrawn at any time and withdrawal must be as easy as giving it.

turns.question: Can I let a large pot of chili cool overnight on the stove before putting it in the fridge?
It is about eight litres. Does the amount matter?
How long does chili keep in the fridge?
Unrelated: what spices go well in a vegetarian chili?
Yesterday I forgot it on the stove for about six hours. Can I still reheat it thoroughly and eat it?
I want to cook a big batch for a party next week. How should I plan it?
How do I cool it quickly next time?
Summarise the food safety rules for this situation.

evidence_plan.reason: USDA FSIS, Leftovers and Food Safety: cooked food left in the danger zone for more than two hours should be discarded; large amounts must be divided to cool quickly.

turns.question: We back up our servers every night. Is that enough for disaster recovery?
We keep backups for 30 days on a separate storage system. Is that okay?
Should we also back up to the cloud?
Unrelated: how do we plan server patching?
Our CEO asks how quickly we could be running again after a ransomware attack. How do we answer?
We have never needed a backup so far. Does that tell us anything?
What should our recovery runbook contain?
Summarise the gaps in our current approach.

evidence_plan.reason: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1: contingency plans, including restoration from backups, must be tested and exercised.

turns.question: I surveyed 200 volunteers about screen time and sleep. Can I conclude that screens cause poor sleep?
The correlation is r = 0.35. Is that strong?
Which statistical test should I report?
Unrelated: how do I format tables in APA style?
Many of the heavy screen users also reported high stress. How does that affect my conclusion?
A journalist wants to quote me saying screens ruin sleep. What should I say?
What study design would let me test the causal claim?
Summarise the limitations section of my report.

evidence_plan.reason: Hernan and Robins, Causal Inference: What If: observational associations can reflect confounding or reverse causation.

turns.question: We plan to plant trees to offset our company's emissions. Is that a solid plan?
We emit about 2,000 tonnes of CO2 per year. How many trees would that take?
Where should we plant them?
Unrelated: how do we get employees involved in sustainability?
A provider offers cheap credits for protecting a forest that was never at risk of being cut. Good deal?
There were large wildfires in the region last year. Does that affect our plan?
How should we report this in our sustainability report?
Summarise what a credible plan should include.

evidence_plan.reason: Oxford Principles for Net Zero Aligned Carbon Offsetting: offsets need additionality and permanence, and emission reductions come first.
